caption: What if you lived on Mercury? Big space news: on 21 November 2026, Europe and Japan's BepiColombo spacecraft entered orbit around Mercury, about 8 years after it launched. From Mercury's surface the Sun looks more than 3 times bigger and up to 7 times brighter. Daytime ground can reach about 430 °C, but with almost no air to hold the heat, nights drop to about -180 °C. A year there lasts just 88 Earth days, yet one sunrise to the next takes 176 Earth days, so a single day lasts two years. From some spots the Sun rises, sets again, then rises again. Even so, deep polar craters that never see sunlight may hide water ice. Plot twist: averaged over time, Mercury is the closest planet to Earth, not Venus (about 1.04 AU vs 1.14 AU), and it's the closest planet to every other planet too. Would YOU live on Mercury? 👇
